standard_prerequisites.name: The gluing category Glue(R -> S, f_1, ..., f_t) and the equivalence of categories with R-modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the formalism that converts the descended object into an R-module and the morphism into a map over R.

standard_prerequisites.name: I-power torsion modules and their vanishing after localizing at the generators of I
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: the hypothesis on kernel and cokernel at statement lines 24887-24888 and used at proof line 24903
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes each localized map an isomorphism, which is what lets the gluing data be assembled.

standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the final statement comparing kernel and cokernel of varphi and psi.

core_obligations: Write I = (f_1, ..., f_t) and observe that each localization varphi_{f_i} is an isomorphism because the kernel and cokernel of varphi are I-power torsion (proof lines 24902-24903).
Conclude that (M', N_{f_i}, varphi_{f_i}, can_{ij}) is an object of the gluing category Glue(R -> S, f_1, ..., f_t) (proof lines 24904-24906).
Apply the equivalence proposition to obtain an R-module M with M' = M tensor_R S and N_{f_i} = M_{f_i}, compatibly with the isomorphisms varphi_{f_i} and can_{ij} (proof lines 24907-24910).

Exhibit the displayed morphism of the gluing category whose first component uses varphi, and conclude that it corresponds to an R-module map psi : M -> N under the equivalence of categories (proof lines 24911-24921).
Verify compatibility: the composition of the base change of psi with the isomorphism M' = M tensor_R S is varphi (proof lines 24922-24924).
Carry out the dual argument for part (2), replacing varphi_{f_i} by varphi_{f_i}^{-1}, to obtain N with N' = N tensor_R S and the map psi : M -> N compatible with varphi (proof lines 24927-24948).
Conclude that the kernel and cokernel of varphi are isomorphic to those of psi, using the neighbourhood equivalence lemma (proof lines 24951-24952).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a flat ring map R -> S and a finitely generated ideal I with R/I -> S/IS an isomorphism, and establishes two dual statements: given an R-module N and an S-module map M' -> N tensor_R S whose kernel and cokernel are I-power torsion, there is an R-module map M -> N and an isomorphism M tensor_R S = M' compatible with these; and symmetrically for a map out of M tensor_R S (source lines 24881-24899). The proof is a genuine application of the gluing equivalence rather than a citation of the conclusion. It writes I = (f_1, ..., f_t) and observes that the localizations at the f_i of the given map are isomorphisms, so that (M', N_{f_i}, varphi_{f_i}, can_{ij}) is an object of the gluing category (proof lines 24902-24906). The equivalence proposition then produces an R-module M with M' = M tensor_R S and N_{f_i} = M_{f_i} compatibly (proof lines 24907-24910). The remaining content is the functoriality step: the displayed morphism in the gluing category whose first component is varphi corresponds to an R-module map psi : M -> N under the equivalence of categories, and the composition of the base change of psi with the isomorphism M' = M tensor_R S is varphi, which is exactly the compatibility (proof lines 24911-24924). Part (2) is carried out as the dual argument with varphi_{f_i}^{-1} replacing varphi_{f_i} (proof lines 24927-24948), and the final kernel-and-cokernel statement is drawn from the neighbourhood equivalence lemma (proof lines 24951-24952). The non-routine content is the translation of a map of glued objects back to a map over R.
